title: tpm2-tools 2a hardening follow-ups: guard the grandchild pid kill, and small test notes (#303 review findings 1-6)
description: Non-blocking findings from the #303 APPROVE. 1 (first, microsecond window but large blast radius): in test/tpm2-tools.test.ts the grandchild test's finally does process.kill(Number(readFileSync(pidFile)), 9); if the timer kills the fake after grandchild.pid exists but before the pid is written, Number('') is 0 and process.kill(0, 9) kills the runner's process group, and a garbled pid is NaN and throws out of the finally. Fix: read the pid, kill only when it is greater than 0, inside a try. 2: comment what the 2.5 s bound measures (the fake's cold start plus spawn plus pid write, about 5x the 474 ms seen under load). 3: have the FIFO child also print statSync(argv[2]).isFIFO(). 5: the comment calls /dev/kmsg root-only but it is mode 0644 (only the O_RDWR open is denied). 6: assert the fileConstants O_NONBLOCK, O_NOCTTY and O_NOFOLLOW are defined, since an undefined one is dropped silently by the bitwise or. Finding 4 (a device node's own open side effects run before fstat refuses it) is unreachable unprivileged and needs no action; recorded only.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The grandchild cleanup kills only a pid greater than 0, inside a try, so no value of the pid file can signal a process group or mask the real failure
adoptToolFile asserts its open flag constants are defined, and the test comments for findings 2, 3 and 5 are corrected

implementationNotes: REVIEW 2026-11-08: round 1 APPROVE WITH CONDITIONS at 7f6fa5a, round 2 APPROVE at 66e9cd900a4fb429643be4de55d4ba1a086ccfec, both from Opus reviewers (model MATCH), relayed by the leader. opum-ai/ward-cli#306 landed as e87da93f6429f2af61b8f476dbade9eeca9197cb. Carried to WCLI-162: the weaker CI witness for the flag constants, and that nothing tests adoptToolFile calls safeOpenFlags.
finalSummary: opum-ai/ward-cli#306 landed as e87da93: the grandchild cleanup signals only a digits-only pid in 1..0x7fffffff inside a try, shown by a recorder test with a real-pid control (removing the pid > 0 check or the upper bound turned only that test red); the grandchild test asserts the pid file holds a positive integer; adoptToolFile opens through safeOpenFlags, which refuses with platform_unsupported when a flag it relies on is not a number, with a test that removes each flag in turn and a real-platform control; comments and the FIFO isFIFO tie-in corrected. Finding 4 recorded only. Follow-ups: WCLI-162.
